factors.value_notes: Partly sourced. The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service's 1978 Mid-Atlantic Bight atlas records adult white grunt at 15–33.6°C, with occasional records in 35°C water but notes fish do not remain long at that extreme; it also describes Florida reef/flat habitat at roughly 6–24 m. This is a broad recorded occurrence range, not a preferred SST band. FishBase reports a model-derived preferred-temperature estimate of 23.4–28°C (mean 25.9°C; 342 spatial cells), which overlaps the configured 22–29°C ideal interval, but it is a distribution/model association rather than a controlled physiological preference or local South Florida catch-response curve. Florida Museum and SAFMC provide species/habitat context but no independent numeric optimum.
